actor_type.description: A single ride request and its lifecycle — the transactional fact whose history-tracked status becomes the CDC changelog, carrying an assigned rider, pickup zone and, once matched, a held driver.

entity_type.description: A rider dimension row — a lookup-join target carrying a name and loyalty tier, assigned to each trip at request time.
A pickup-zone dimension row — a lookup-join target carrying a name and zone type (commercial, transit, residential, campus) for each trip's origin.

current_state.description: A newly arrived trip binding its rider and pickup zone, then searching for an available driver.
The trip waiting to seize a driver from the shared fleet, holding in the queue when every driver is busy — this wait is the emergent match-time.
A driver has been matched and is driving to the rider, who then either boards or turns out to be a no-show.
The rider has boarded and the ride is underway toward drop-off.
The ride finished and the driver was released — the terminal success outcome.
The rider was a no-show, releasing the driver without a ride — the terminal cancellation outcome.

journey_type.description: The trip lifecycle from request through matching, pickup and the ride to a completed or cancelled outcome — the state machine whose status changes drive the SCD-2 / CDC changelog.

discipline.description: Waiters promoted by highest declared priority, ties by earliest enqueue.
A newly-arriving higher-priority actor displaces a lower-priority holder; 1-server queues only.

on_full.description: The seize waits in the queue for a slot to free.
The seize is rejected immediately and routed to its on_rejected handler.
The seize resamples a delay and is retried.
The seize is routed to its on_reroute handler.

resource_type.description: A driver in the finite metro fleet — a seizable resource a trip holds from match through drop-off; all drivers share one queue, so riders wait when every driver is busy.

scenario_description: A single-region ride-sharing marketplace over one week: riders request trips through the day, a small finite driver fleet picks them up and frees up for the next request, and each trip walks a lifecycle from request to a completed or cancelled outcome — rendered as a per-trip change-data-capture changelog in which rider match-wait emerges from a peaking demand stream contending for a fixed fleet.
